QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_30

question.text: The terms of Co-Investment by a Manager or Sponsor in an investee company through CIV or PMS route, compared with the terms of investment by the AIF itself, shall:

answer.text: Be more favourable to the manager/sponsor as a perquisite.
Be structured so the manager exits first.
NOT be more favourable than the terms of investment for the AIF; and exit terms (including timing) must be identical to the AIF's exit.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 11.5: terms of co-investment shall NOT be more favourable than the terms for the AIF; and exit terms (including timing) shall be IDENTICAL to the AIF's exit. The manager cannot advise any investor other than clients of the Co-investment Portfolio Manager under SEBI (PMS) Regulations for investment in the same investee. The Trap: 'More favourable to manager' violates fairness; 'exits first' violates identical-exit requirement; 'guaranteed IRR' is not permitted. Cross-Exam Context: Same rule in XIX-C/D. Important: SEBI September 9, 2025 amendment opened an in-AIF CIV-scheme route for Cat I/II co-invest — Cat III typically uses this less. Manager's Pro-Tip: Structure any Cat III co-invest with a strict pari-passu Term Sheet: same allocation ratio, same exit date, same valuation haircut on redemption — ensures full compliance and reduces the risk of SEBI interpreting 'identical exit' strictly during inspection.
